AC:
Deliverables, all inside a new `econsent/` project honoring the utils conventions (project-local `.venv` via ./create_pipenv.sh, `make test` fast/no-network, `make all-tests` for the slow suite, `.www/blurb.md` + `make index`):
1. A literate END test that drives fetch -> mention extraction -> sentiment -> price alignment -> correlation -> report over a small offline fixture corpus and asserts a reproducible ranked report.
2. Idempotent ingest behind an `ArticleSource` interface storing normalized articles (stable id, section, theme labels, publish timestamp with timezone, body text, fetch provenance); the retention and legal posture chosen in D1/D6 is honored in code, and the store is git-ignored.
3. Company mention extraction evaluated on a hand-labeled dev set with reported precision/recall, plus mention-to-ticker resolution through SEC company_tickers.json/sec-cik-mapper and OpenFIGI with a name-mismatch veto and a log of unresolved mentions.
4. Entity-level sentiment from at least two scorers behind one interface, each evaluated on a hand-labeled gold set of mention/sentiment pairs with reported macro-F1; explicit market-prediction content excluded per D10 with measured precision of the exclusion rule.
5. Split- and dividend-adjusted daily price history cached locally for the resolved universe, plus benchmark/index returns, with a per-ticker coverage report.
6. A market-model abnormal-return panel at +5/+21/+252 trading days (buy-and-hold abnormal return at the long horizon), with tests that fail on look-ahead or on misaligned publication-to-first-tradable-session mapping.
7. Inference reporting, per section/theme x horizon x scorer cell, the effect size, n, Newey-West HAC p-value (with Kolari-Pynnonen clustering adjustment) and Benjamini-Hochberg q-value; cells that do not clear FDR are labeled as such rather than dropped.
8. A ranked markdown + CSV report of sections/themes by absolute correlation at each horizon.
9. A placebo run (shuffled sentiment) and a pre-event window leakage check, both reported alongside the real result.
10. One-command reproduction from the cached corpus and price snapshot, with pinned requirements and a manifest of input hashes.
A statistically null finding satisfies this AC provided items 1-10 hold; the pipeline and the honest table are the deliverable, not a positive correlation.

Body.raw:
Use an Economist subscription to farm sentiment from ordinary articles (explicitly ignoring the magazine's own market calls and forecast columns). Extract company mentions and the sentiment directed at each mention, then post-dict: measure whether mention sentiment correlates with the mentioned company's subsequent abnormal return at roughly 1 week / 1 month / 1 year. Deliverable is a ranked table of article sections and themes by absolute correlation strength, with honest significance numbers. Goal: discover which Economist coverage, if any, has predictive power for equity moves.

WHY post-diction rather than a live signal: the question is measurement -- does this corpus carry equity-relevant information at all -- so the pipeline is built for reproducible historical study, not trading. No execution, no portfolio construction, no real-time inference is in scope.

## Groomed technical approach (research pass, Aug 2026)

Access. There is no public full-text Economist RSS. Section RSS and sitemaps yield headline, teaser and timestamp only; full text requires a subscriber session, and the Economist Group terms of use forbid bypassing the paywall and restrict content to personal, non-commercial use. Design consequence: an `ArticleSource` interface with swappable backends -- free metadata crawl, browser-cookie session, Playwright login, manual print-edition export (app EPUB/PDF), institutional ProQuest/EBSCO access -- so the legal posture is a configuration choice instead of a rewrite. The subscriber digital archive reaches back to 1997, which is the only realistic way to get enough non-overlapping one-year windows.

NLP. Company mentions via spaCy ORG NER (`en_core_web_trf`) compared against GLiNER on a hand-labeled dev set. Mention to security resolution via an alias table plus SEC `company_tickers.json` / `sec-cik-mapper` and the OpenFIGI `/v3/mapping` endpoint, with a name-mismatch veto rather than emitting a plausible wrong ticker. Sentiment must be entity-level, not document-level: Economist paragraphs routinely praise one firm while damning another in the same sentence. Candidate scorers behind one interface -- VADER as a floor, the Loughran-McDonald finance dictionary, FinBERT and FinBERT-tone, `deberta-v3-base-absa` (target-aware; the strongest fine-tuned macro-F1 in 2025-26 target-based financial sentiment benchmarks), optionally a local LLM -- all evaluated against a hand-labeled gold set of mention/sentiment pairs.

Market data. An adapter interface over Stooq (free, keyless), Tiingo, Alpha Vantage, or EODHD (paid, deepest history and widest exchange coverage); yfinance is prototype-only because it scrapes an unofficial endpoint. Requirements are split- and dividend-adjusted daily bars, delisting and ticker-change history, and an index or factor benchmark for normal returns.

Statistics. Standard event-study shape: a market-model estimation window of 120-250 trading days ending before publication, abnormal returns cumulated to +5, +21 and +252 trading days (buy-and-hold abnormal return at the long horizon). Overlapping return windows require Newey-West HAC standard errors; the print edition publishes weekly so event dates cluster, requiring a Kolari-Pynnonen cross-sectional variance adjustment; the section x theme x horizon x scorer grid requires Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control. Look-ahead control is a first-class test target: Thursday-evening London publication maps to a specific first tradable session per listing venue.

Honest prior: a 2026 QLoRA benchmark of financial sentiment models found that none of 28 model-horizon return-predictability tests survived FDR correction. A rigorous null result is a likely and acceptable outcome here; the validated pipeline plus the honest table is the deliverable.

## Tracker choice (frequentcommits)

Sequential WorkItems on one branch for scaffolding, the END test, and Economist access, because those share one store schema and one legal decision. Phase 2 (NLP pipeline) and phase 3 (market data) are the two genuinely independent, context-heavy domains and are the intended `add-subtodo` split once the panel row schema is frozen; they may be authorized to run in parallel. Phases 4-5 (inference, reporting) return to parent WorkItems. Default stays sequential unless the user asks for fan-out.

## Unresolved decisions -- need user input, deliberately not guessed

D1 Legal posture. Pick one: (a) personal-research only, local-only, derived text never redistributed; (b) institutional/library access (ProQuest, EBSCO) whose license may permit text mining; (c) licensed commercial data. Also: is any output ever meant to be published or committed to a public repo?

D2 Subscription authentication. Browser-cookie import (which browser and profile), Playwright headless login with credentials from a secret store, manual print-edition export, or institutional proxy? Do usable credentials exist, is 2FA on the account, and where may the secret live?

D3 Market data source and budget. Free and keyless (Stooq), free tier with key (Tiingo, Alpha Vantage), or paid (EODHD, roughly USD 20/month for 30+ years and 60+ exchanges)? Any spend at all?

D4 Universe and benchmark. US-only (S&P 500 plus SEC registrants) or global -- the Economist covers a great many LSE, Euronext, TSE and emerging-market firms? Which benchmark per listing venue, ADR versus local line for foreign issuers, and what happens to mentions of private, state-owned or acquired companies?

D5 Horizons. Confirm 1wk/1mo/1yr as +5/+21/+252 trading days. Add the literature's clean +1 and +3 day announcement windows and a pre-event window as a leakage check?

D6 Corpus depth and retention. How far back -- the full 1997 archive, or a bounded recent window? Retain raw article HTML and full text indefinitely, retain only derived features (hashes, spans, scores) after extraction, or auto-expire raw text after N days? Where does the store live, and is encryption at rest required? (Store must be git-ignored regardless.)

D7 Committed artifacts. Code and synthetic fixtures only, or are short real article excerpts acceptable in test fixtures? This decides whether the END test fixtures are hand-written pastiche or captured text.

D8 Statistical ambition. With perhaps 1-3k resolvable company mentions per year, the one-year horizon offers only a handful of independent windows. Confirm that a rigorously produced null result counts as success, versus wanting an exploratory ranking that reports raw correlations without significance gating.

D9 Sentiment compute budget. Local CPU models only (FinBERT, DeBERTa-ABSA), a local LLM via ollama, or a paid LLM API whose cost scales with mention count?

D10 Exclusion rule for "explicit market predictions". Drop whole columns (Buttonwood, Free exchange, market reports, Economics briefs) or detect forecast sentences individually? The former is cheap and auditable; the latter needs its own labeled sample.

## USER INPUT (2026-08-23): Prior art for subscriber-credential downloaders

Existing open-source tools for downloading Economist content with subscriber credentials:

**Script Downloaders (require subscription credentials):**
- [nino/economist-downloader](https://github.com/nino/economist-downloader): Downloads weekly print edition to EPUB
- [MikeInnes/economist-ebook](https://github.com/MikeInnes/economist-ebook): Node.js, Calibre integration, EPUB/Kindle output
- [calebbrgr/Economist2Epub](https://github.com/calebbrgr/Economist2Epub): Python-based, EPUB output

**Pre-compiled archives (rolling community uploads):**
- [blleng/The-Economist](https://github.com/blleng/The-Economist): Updates weekly, last 12 issues in EPUB/MOBI/PDF
- [hehonghui/awesome-english-ebooks](https://github.com/hehonghui/awesome-english-ebooks): Structured by year

**Impact on approach:**
- D2 (authentication) informed: use existing downloader prior art rather than building from scratch
- Prefer nino/economist-downloader or calebbrgr/Economist2Epub (Python) as the ArticleSource backend
- EPUB output already structures articles by section — can parse directly
- Pre-compiled archives potentially useful for deep historical corpus (licensing TBD for ML training)

LongSummary.raw:
A research pipeline that mines entity-level sentiment out of ordinary Economist articles and tests whether it post-dicts equity moves for the companies mentioned. Ordinary coverage only: the magazine's own market calls and forecast columns (Buttonwood, Free exchange, market reports) are deliberately excluded, because the question is whether incidental journalistic tone carries signal, not whether explicit predictions do. The output is a ranked table of Economist sections and themes by absolute correlation strength at roughly 1 week, 1 month and 1 year horizons, with effect size, sample count and multiple-testing-corrected significance beside every cell.

Access is the first hard constraint. The Economist publishes no full-text RSS; section feeds and sitemaps give only headline, teaser and timestamp, and full text requires a subscriber session, while the Economist Group terms of use forbid paywall circumvention and limit content to personal, non-commercial use. The design therefore hides retrieval behind an `ArticleSource` interface with swappable backends -- free metadata crawl, browser-cookie session, Playwright login, manual print-edition export, institutional ProQuest or EBSCO access -- so the legal posture stays a configuration choice. The subscriber digital archive reaches back to 1997, which matters because one-year horizons need many years of non-overlapping windows.

The NLP half extracts company mentions with spaCy ORG NER (`en_core_web_trf`) benchmarked against GLiNER on a hand-labeled dev set, then resolves each mention to a security through an alias table, SEC `company_tickers.json` / `sec-cik-mapper`, and the OpenFIGI `/v3/mapping` endpoint, vetoing a mapping on gross name mismatch rather than emitting a plausible wrong ticker. Sentiment is scored per mention, not per document, because Economist prose praises and damns different firms in one paragraph; scorers sit behind one interface (VADER as a floor, the Loughran-McDonald finance dictionary, FinBERT and FinBERT-tone, target-aware `deberta-v3-base-absa`, optionally a local LLM) and are ranked on a hand-labeled gold set of mention/sentiment pairs.

The market half pulls split- and dividend-adjusted daily bars through a provider adapter (Stooq keyless, Tiingo, Alpha Vantage, or paid EODHD; yfinance prototype-only) and computes market-model abnormal returns over a 120-250 day estimation window, cumulated to +5, +21 and +252 trading days with buy-and-hold abnormal return at the long horizon. Inference takes overlapping windows seriously: Newey-West HAC standard errors, a Kolari-Pynnonen adjustment for the weekly print edition clustering event dates, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control across the section by theme by horizon by scorer grid. Look-ahead control -- mapping Thursday-evening London publication to the correct first tradable session -- is enforced by tests, not convention.

A null result is an expected and acceptable outcome: a 2026 QLoRA benchmark found no financial-sentiment model-horizon return-predictability test survived FDR correction, and with perhaps one to three thousand resolvable company mentions per year the one-year horizon has few independent observations. Deliverable is the validated pipeline plus an honest table, not a trading strategy; execution, portfolio construction and live inference are out of scope. Grooming leaves ten decisions open for the user, the load-bearing ones being legal posture and authentication method, market data provider and budget, ticker universe (US-only versus the many non-US firms the Economist covers), raw-text retention policy, and whether a rigorous null result counts as success.

Expected red until phase 5 lands.

[LOCAP] Corpus inventory report: article counts per section per year and publish-hour distribution against London and New York market sessions. Run-and-report; the numbers feed the statistical-power decision D8.
[MIDCAP] Hand-label a dev set of roughly 100 company mentions drawn from the ingested corpus (character spans plus canonical company name), stored as a versioned fixture for NER evaluation.

[HICAP] Mention extraction exemplar: MentionExtractor interface with spaCy en_core_web_trf ORG NER versus GLiNER, plus an evaluation harness reporting precision/recall/F1 on the dev set. Pick the default and document why.

[MIDCAP] Mention-to-security resolver: alias table plus SEC company_tickers.json / sec-cik-mapper plus OpenFIGI /v3/mapping, with a gross name-mismatch veto instead of a plausible wrong ticker, on-disk cache, and an unresolved-mention log for manual alias curation.
[MIDCAP] Hand-label a gold set of roughly 200 mention-sentiment pairs (positive/neutral/negative directed at that mention, not the article) for sentiment scorer evaluation.

[HICAP] Entity-level sentiment exemplar: SentimentScorer interface plus two implementations (VADER context-window baseline and target-aware deberta-v3-base-absa), macro-F1 evaluation harness against the gold set, and a score cache keyed by article_id, mention span and scorer version.

[MIDCAP] Roll out the remaining scorers behind the same interface: Loughran-McDonald finance dictionary, FinBERT, FinBERT-tone, and optionally a local LLM per decision D9. Extend the evaluation table; no interface changes.

[MIDCAP] Explicit-market-prediction exclusion per decision D10: column/section blocklist (Buttonwood, Free exchange, market reports) plus optional forecast-sentence detector, with a labeled sample and measured precision of the exclusion.

[MIDCAP] Price data adapter: PriceSource interface plus the backend chosen in D3, split- and dividend-adjusted daily bars, ticker-change and delisting handling, on-disk parquet cache, rate limiting, and an offline fixture backend for tests.

[MIDCAP] Benchmark and factor returns: index series per listing venue per decision D4, optionally Fama-French factors from the Ken French library, cached alongside prices for market-model normal returns.
[LOCAP] Price data-quality checks: missing bars, zero-volume days, extreme-return outliers, and per-ticker coverage against the mention dates. Run-and-report with escalation of any fix.

[HICAP] Return alignment and abnormal-return engine: publish timestamp to first tradable session per venue, market-model estimation window of 120-250 trading days ending before the event, AR/CAR at +5/+21/+252 trading days and BHAR at the long horizon. Look-ahead prevention enforced by tests.

[MIDCAP] Panel builder: one row per mention and horizon carrying sentiment, section, theme, ticker, size bucket, CAR and controls, rebuilt deterministically from cache. Freezing this schema is the gate for splitting the NLP and market-data phases into subtodos.

[HICAP] Inference layer: per-cell correlation and rank information coefficient with Newey-West HAC standard errors for overlapping windows, Kolari-Pynnonen adjustment for weekly print-edition event clustering, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control across the section x theme x horizon x scorer grid.
[MIDCAP] Robustness suite: shuffled-sentiment placebo, pre-event window leakage check, winsorization, subperiod splits, and scorer-swap stability, each reported next to the main result.

[MIDCAP] Ranked report generator: markdown plus CSV listing sections and themes ordered by absolute correlation per horizon with n, effect size, Newey-West p and BH q, labeling cells that fail FDR rather than dropping them.

[LOCAP] Finish wiring: make test and make all-tests targets, README and .www/blurb.md, root index refresh via make index, pinned requirements, and the input-hash manifest for one-command reproduction.
